t: Under a fire policy, the duty of disclosure of material facts continues during the currency of the policy by virtue of
o: Condition 3 of the policy relating to alteration of risk
Condition 15 relating to reinstatement of sum insured
e: Utmost good faith applies at inception and during the currency (Condition 3 requires sanction for alteration of trade, unoccupancy beyond 30 days and change of interest); the declaration in the proposal makes it a contractual duty.

t: The fire rate under SFSP comprises which components?
o: Basic, kutcha and silent risk rates
e: The notes state the fire rate comprises FLEXA (fire, lightning, explosion, aircraft), RSMD and STFI rates; the rates currently follow the IIB rates published in December 2021.

t: A seasonal godown is insured for 3 months. Sum insured ₹50 lakh, annual rate ₹2.00‰. The premium is
e: Annual premium = 50,00,000 × 2/1000 = ₹10,000; for a period not exceeding 3 months the short-period scale is 40%, so ₹4,000.

t: An annual SFSP policy (premium ₹12,000) is cancelled at the insured's request after exactly 4 months. The refund due is
e: Cancellation at the insured's option: premium retained at the short-period scale – 50% for 4 months = ₹6,000 retained, so ₹6,000 refunded.

t: Damage caused to insured property by the pressure waves of an aircraft travelling at supersonic speed is
o: Excluded under the Aircraft Damage peril
e: Aircraft Damage covers loss caused by aircraft, other aerial or space devices and articles dropped therefrom, excluding damage caused by pressure waves.

t: An SFSP policy with sum insured ₹600 crore at one location sustains a flood loss of ₹80 lakh. The excess applicable is
e: For SI above ₹100 crore up to ₹1,500 crore per location: 5% of the claim subject to a minimum of ₹5 lakh; 5% of ₹80 lakh = ₹4 lakh, so the minimum ₹5 lakh applies.

t: A sole proprietor insured under SFSP sells his factory to a company; two months later a fire occurs and no endorsement was obtained. The claim is
o: Not payable, as the interest in the property passed otherwise than by will or operation of law
e: Condition 3(d): the insurance ceases to attach if the interest passes from the insured otherwise than by will or operation of law; a fire policy is not freely assignable.

t: Condition 7 of the SFSP policy empowers the insurer, on the happening of loss, to
o: Repudiate the claim if the insured obstructs the surveyor
Recover the premium for the unexpired period
Enter and take possession of the premises and deal with or sell the salvage, without being deemed to have accepted abandonment
Cancel the policy with immediate effect
e: Condition 7: insurer may enter the premises, take possession of and dispose of property; the insured cannot abandon property to the insurer. Obstruction forfeits benefits.

t: Under Condition 15 of the SFSP policy, the pro-rata premium for reinstatement of the sum insured after a loss is
o: Waived if the loss is less than 10% of SI
Collected separately before the claim is paid
Deducted from the net claim amount payable for the period from date of loss to expiry
e: Condition 15: cover is maintained to the full SI; pro-rata premium from date of loss to expiry on the loss amount is deducted from the claim, unless the insured opts not to reinstate the SI.

t: Long-term fire policies for a period exceeding 12 months may be issued only for
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). AIFT General Rule 3: policies exceeding 12 months shall not be issued except for dwellings; refund is not allowed for reduction of SI under such long-term policies.

t: Under a Reinstatement Value policy, adequacy of the sum insured for applying average is tested with reference to the cost of reinstatement
o: As on the date of reinstatement
As on the date of inception
As on the date of loss
As on the date of the last renewal
e: RIV special provision 2: if the cost of reinstating the whole property at the time of reinstatement exceeds the SI, the insured bears a rateable proportion; under MV policies adequacy is as on the date of loss.

t: Leakage and Contamination cover under AIFT applies to
o: Oils and chemicals in land tanks only
e: The extension applies to oils and chemicals only; each claim carries an excess of 1% per tank with a minimum of ₹60,000, and rates are ₹5‰/₹6‰ (leakage) or ₹10‰/₹12‰ (leakage and contamination).

t: A tenant who is not obliged to pay rent for the damaged premises takes alternative accommodation at ₹30,000 per month; his earlier rent was ₹18,000. The additional rent recoverable per month under the Alternative Accommodation add-on is
e: If the tenant is not obliged to pay rent for the damaged premises, additional rent = new rent − old rent = ₹12,000; if he must continue paying the old rent, the full new rent is the additional rent.

t: A declaration policy cannot be issued for
o: Stocks of raw material in a godown
e: AIFT Rule 14(f): declaration policies are not permitted for short-period insurance, stocks undergoing process, or stocks at railway sidings.

t: Stock of ₹4 lakh is covered by an SFSP policy for ₹1 lakh and a declaration policy for ₹2 lakh. A loss of ₹3 lakh occurs. The declaration policy pays
e: The SFSP pays 3 × 1/4 = ₹0.75 lakh. The excess of stock value over the SFSP SI is ₹3 lakh, which exceeds the declaration SI, so the SI is used: 3 × 2/4 = ₹1.5 lakh; total ₹2.25 lakh.

t: The Designation of Property clause provides that
o: Property can only be insured under the item 'stock'
The insured must designate a nominee for the claim
The property must be designated by a licensed valuer
The insurer accepts the designation under which the property is entered in the insured's books of account
e: The clause settles disputes about which item covers a property (e.g. oil held as stock versus machinery) by following the insured's books of account.

t: In the AIFT sequence for computation of rate, the discount for a voluntary deductible is applied
o: Only on the STFI portion of the rate
On the basic rate before the sprinkler reduction
On the total premium calculated at the final rate after all other adjustments
e: Rule 21: basic rate → 5% sprinkler reduction → deletion of STFI/RSMTD → kutcha extra → claims experience discount/loading → FEA discount → voluntary deductible discount on the total premium.

t: Under Bharat Griha Raksha, the sum insured for the home building is arrived at as
o: Carpet area in square metres multiplied by the rate of cost of construction at the policy commencement date
Market value of the flat including land
Built-up area multiplied by the circle rate
Reinstatement value declared by a valuer
e: BGR building SI = carpet area × prevailing cost of construction; general contents are on replacement cost and valuable contents on agreed value.

t: Under an EAR policy, earthquake cover is granted on first-loss basis for 20% of the sum insured. The EQ premium chargeable is
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). First-loss EQ in project policies: 20% of SI attracts 50% of the tariff rate; 10% of SI attracts 40% of the tariff rate. EQ rates are applied pro-rata to the policy period.

t: Which of the following best describes a 'contributory' fire hazard?
o: Locked or inaccessible premises which allow a fire to spread unchecked
e: Originating hazards are causes of fire (electrical, smoking, welding, sparks); contributory hazards increase the probability of spread or loss, such as combustible construction, absence of people, locked premises and exposure.

t: A risk estimate of loss that gives due consideration to fire protection devices, construction, size and occupancy is called
e: Maximum possible loss is the worst-case 'shock loss' ignoring protections; PML/MPL considers protection, construction, size and occupancy. A risk with a lower PML is a better risk.

t: Under an IAR policy, piping and cables up to what percentage of the MBD sum insured need not be considered for premium calculation of the MBD portion?
e: Piping and cables up to 15% of the MBD SI are excluded for MBD premium computation, though the MBD SI and coverage remain 100%.

t: Previous year's turnover ₹200 crore, rate of gross profit 30%. Due to a fire the current year's turnover falls to ₹100 crore with the same facilities. The rate of GP for the current year works out to
e: GP = 200 × 30% = ₹60 crore and remains constant as standing charges and net profit do not vary with turnover; 60/100 = 60%.

t: Under a Fire LOP policy, increased cost of working is payable subject to
o: A maximum of the loss of gross profit thereby avoided, and under-insurance in the ratio of insured to total standing charges
A maximum of 10% of the sum insured
No limit, provided it is reasonably incurred
e: ICW is payable up to the amount of GP loss saved; it is subject to under-insurance (ICW × insured standing charges / total standing charges) and any savings in standing charges are deducted.

t: Which policy covers transit of plant and machinery from the manufacturer's warehouse through erection and testing up to commissioning?
e: MCE runs from the time the equipment leaves the manufacturer's warehouse to final commissioning and combines marine (all risks) and EAR coverage.

t: A CAR policy period ends on
o: The end of the maintenance period
The date of expiry or the date of handing over the works to the principal, whichever is earlier
The date of final payment to the contractor
e: CAR ends on DOE/handing over to the principal; EAR ends on DOE/date of commercial production.

t: The EAR sum insured is adjustable on completion on the basis of actual values of
o: Prime cost of plant and machinery only
Construction cost, freight, customs duties and handling charges, but not prime cost of materials
Nothing; the SI is fixed at inception
e: SI adjustment on completion takes actuals for construction cost, freight, customs duty and handling charges; increase/decrease in prime cost of material is not taken into account.

t: An IAR policy insured's loss is ₹50 lakh and under-insurance is found to be 12%. The under-insurance deduction is
o: Nil, as under-insurance up to 15% is waived
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). IAR special condition: under-insurance up to 15% is waived; if it exceeds 15%, the full under-insurance is applied.

t: Under the Air Freight extension of a project policy, an additional excess applies equal to
e: Air freight: reinstatement of SI after loss possible; additional excess of 5% of the air freight incurred.

t: The term 'major perils' in project insurance refers to
o: AOG perils, collapse and wet risks
e: Major perils = AOG + collapse + wet risk; a higher excess (10% of claim, minimum testing excess, cap ₹5 crore) applies to them.

t: A flood damages a bridge under construction on 1 August; a second flood damages the same works on 5 August. For excess purposes,
o: No excess applies to the second loss
A single excess applies, as the perils were not separated by 7 consecutive clear days
e: Losses are separate incidents only if separated by 7 consecutive days of freedom from the peril; otherwise one excess applies.

t: For an EAR policy with sum insured ₹8 crore, the maximum TPL cover that can be granted is
e: For project SI up to ₹10 crore, TPL may be granted up to ₹1 crore; above ₹10 crore it is 10% of completely erected value or ₹10 crore, whichever is lower.

t: For a thermal power plant, the testing period ends when
o: Steam is first introduced into the turbine
The TG set is synchronised with the grid
The TG set operates at full load for a continuous period of 72 hours or on expiry of the testing period, whichever is earlier
e: End of testing: 72 hours continuous full-load operation or policy expiry of the testing period, whichever is earlier; maximum testing period for thermal plants is 6 months.

t: Where premium instalments are allowed under a project policy, the last instalment must be collected
o: 6 months before expiry of the policy
On the date of commencement of testing
e: Instalments are allowed if the period exceeds 12 months; minimum interval 3 months; last instalment 6 months before expiry; first instalment 5% more than the others.

t: An Insurance Ombudsman can entertain a complaint where the value of the claim, including expenses, does not exceed:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). The limit was raised to ₹50 lakh by the amended Insurance Ombudsman Rules.

t: Under DE5 wording, which cost remains excluded?
o: Rectification (redesign) charges of the defective part
Damage to the machine in which the defective part is fitted
Cost of the defective part itself
e: DE5 pays for surrounding property, connected machine, the machine containing the defect and the cost of the defective part, but not the cost of improving/redesigning the defective part.

t: The London Engineering Group wording LEG2/96 is broadly equivalent to
e: LEG1 ≈ DE1 (outright exclusion); LEG2 ≈ DE4 (excludes defective part and access costs); LEG3 ≈ DE5 (full cover except improvement costs).

t: In an ALOP claim, the surveyor must
o: Settle multiple claims for each delay event
Segregate insured delay from uninsured delay and compute the GP loss for the insured delay only
Apply depreciation to the project cost
Pay the full indemnity period GP irrespective of cause
e: ALOP responds only to delay caused by physical damage admissible under CAR/EAR; only one claim is payable, and uninsured delays (e.g. financial or supplier delays) are segregated.

t: The basis of sum insured under an MBD policy is
o: Written down value as per books
Current new replacement value including freight, customs duty and erection cost
e: SI under MBD, EEI, BPP and CPM is the current new replacement value (CNRV) of the equipment; increase/decrease of SI mid-term is on short-period scale.

t: Which machine is on the declined list for MBD cover?
e: Declined list includes stone crushers, rolling mill stands, lined vessels, radios/TVs, imported machinery not repairable in India, cupolas, pumps with glass/rubber impellers, pipelines, computers (to be covered under EEI) and portable equipment.

t: A 3-year-old wire rope of a crane is replaced in an MBD claim at a cost of ₹2,00,000. The amount payable before excess is
e: Ropes in lifts, cranes and ropeways attract depreciation of 15% per year subject to a maximum of 75%: 3 × 15% = 45%, so 2,00,000 × 55% = ₹1,10,000.

t: The maximum escalation permissible under an MBD policy is
e: MBD escalation: selected percentage not exceeding 25%, additional premium at 50% of the full rate on the increase, pro-rata average continues to apply.

t: Under EEI, the excess for computers differs
o: It is a uniform 5% of the claim
Between office use and industrial use
Between equipment valued up to ₹1 lakh and above ₹1 lakh, and for the hard disk compared to other parts
e: EEI excess is different for equipment valued up to ₹1 lakh and above ₹1 lakh, and a separate excess applies to the hard disk.

t: Which warranty is attached to a Boiler and Pressure Plant policy?
o: The boiler is kept idle for at least 30 days a year
The boiler is operated only in a single shift
The insured maintains a stand-by boiler
The boiler is inspected annually by boiler inspectors and operated by attendants holding valid certificates of competency
e: BPP warranties: annual inspection by inspectors and operation by certified attendants; add-ons include escalation, express/air freight, surrounding property, TPL and additional customs duty.

t: The IRDAI portal through which a policyholder can escalate an unresolved grievance against an insurer is:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Bima Bharosa (formerly IGMS) is the grievance portal; Bima Sugam is the marketplace, Bima Vahak the women-led distribution channel and Bima Vistaar the combined rural product.

t: CPM insurance is best described as
o: An all-risks policy with exclusion of electrical and mechanical breakdown
A motor policy for construction vehicles
A long-term policy for mobile cranes
e: CPM covers sudden unforeseen physical loss (fire, theft, RSMD, STFI, EQ, collision, accidental damage) but excludes breakdown, consumables, transit between locations, wear and tear and war.

t: Under a DOS policy, damage to stock is excluded if the stoppage of the refrigeration plant following an accident lasts
e: DOS excludes damage from stoppage of any section of the plant for less than 24 hours and damage where the chamber temperature does not exceed 40°F (4.4°C).

t: The maximum refund of premium under an MLOP policy on account of difference in gross profit is
e: MLOP premium refund due to difference in actual versus insured GP is limited to 50%, similar to the declaration refund limit.

t: For a 250 MW combined-cycle gas-based power plant under EAR, the minimum deductible for a testing-period claim is
o: 10% of the claim subject to a minimum of ₹50 lakh
5% of the claim subject to a minimum of ₹60 lakh
5% of the claim subject to a minimum of ₹125 lakh
5% of the claim subject to a minimum of ₹100 lakh
e: Combined-cycle/gas plants: 50–200 MW – min ₹60 lakh testing/₹20 lakh normal; 200–300 MW – ₹100 lakh/₹50 lakh; 300 MW and above – ₹125 lakh/₹75 lakh.

t: The minimum deductible for the boom section of a crane under a CPM policy is
o: 20% of the claim amount subject to a minimum of ₹25,000
10% of the claim amount subject to a minimum of ₹5,000
e: CPM circular: boom section 20% of claim, minimum ₹25,000; Group V machinery ₹2,500 flat; other groups per the value-band table.
